title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 4 begins the determination of M_{11}(4), the moduli of elliptic curves with full level-4 structure, over bases where 2 is invertible. It continues the previous section, where level 2 was handled through the degree-3 étale cover J and the Legendre-type parametrization, and the duplication map f_2^t was computed.

(38) Put M = _4E. It is a finite étale group scheme locally isomorphic to (Z/4)^2, equivalently a locally free (Z/4)_S-module of rank 2 on S_ét.

(39) There is a short exact sequence 0 -> M_0 -> M -> M_0 -> 0.
- The second map is reduction mod 2, M -> M/2M.
- The first map is the inclusion of 2M = _2E.
- Their composite (M -> M_0 -> M) is 2·id_M.
- M_0 = M ⊗_{Z/4} F_2 ≅ _2E, the isomorphism being induced by multiplication by 2.

Strategy: classify M by first giving M_0, then the extra datum needed to recover M.

(40) A locally free rank-2 F_2-module M_0 is the same as a degree-3 étale cover J. Here J is the set of nonzero sections of M_0^* (identifiable with the nonzero 2-torsion points via the Weil pairing). One has M_0 = V_J(F_2) = Ker(F_2^J --sum--> F_2) ≅ F_2^J / F_2(diagonal); the two descriptions agree because |J| = 3 is odd. This is the S_3 = GL_2(F_2) dictionary.

(41) Given M_0, the M lifting it form a torsor P under V_J(M_0) ≅ End_{F_2,S}(M_0). Group-theoretically this works as follows.
- Ker(GL_2(Z/4) -> GL_2(F_2)) = 1 + 2M_2 ≅ M_2(F_2) is abelian.
- GL_2(Z/4) -> S_3 splits, since S_3 lifts to GL_2(Z).
- So there is a canonical base point V_J(Z/4) = Ker((Z/4)^J -> Z/4).
- The other forms are classified by H^1(S, End(M_0)), with End(M_0) twisted by M_0.

Grothendieck then decomposes End(M_0) ≅ M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω, where ω is the degree-2 étale 'cover of orientations' attached to J (S_3/A_3, i.e. the square root of the discriminant). As an F_2[S_3]-module, M_0 is the 2-dimensional projective irreducible (Steinberg) module. End(M_0) = V⊗V is then projective of dimension 4 with composition factors 1, 1, V. Hence it is P(1) ⊕ V, and P(1) = F_2[S_3/A_3] = F_2^ω.

Consequence (not written, but implied): H^1(S, End M_0) = H^1(S, _2E) ⊕ H^1(ω, Z/2) by Shapiro's lemma. So the lifting data split into an _2E-torsor (halving data) and a double cover of the orientation cover ω (square-root data).

(42) A pinning (épinglage) of M, i.e. an isomorphism (Z/4)^2_S ≅ _4E, is equivalent to:
- a trivialization of J (level-2 structure), plus
- a section of the torsor P.

The next page identifies P as the inverse image of id_{M_0} in the extension 0 -> V_J(M_0) -> V_J(M) -> V_J(M_0) -> 0 obtained by applying the exact functor V_J to (39). This exhibits M_{11}(4) -> M_{11}(2) as a torsor under (Z/2)^4 = ker(GL_2(Z/4) -> GL_2(F_2)), described concretely.
errors: (40) 'J ≅ M_0^*' is loose: J is the degree-3 cover of nonzero sections of M_0^* (or of M_0 via the Weil pairing), not M_0^* itself.
The isomorphism M ⊗ F_2 ≅ _2E is via multiplication by 2; the page leaves this implicit. In the diagram the arrow M -> M is 2·id, which factors as M -> M_0 ↪ M.

The statement 'data of M equivalent to M_0 plus a torsor under End(M_0)' tacitly uses the canonical base point V_J(Z/4) coming from the splitting GL_2(Z/4) -> S_3. The torsor is canonical only relative to this; it is made explicit on the next page. No real error.

ideas.what: Classifying rank-2 free Z/4-local systems (4-torsion of E) by the mod-2 reduction plus a torsor under End(M_0) (dévissage of GL_2(Z/4) via the abelian kernel M_2(F_2))
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1 dévissage / forms of local systems; tower X(4) -> X(2) as a torsor under Γ(2)/Γ(4)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Giraud-style nonabelian cohomology; classical modular curves)
ideas.where_published: general torsor/H^1 formalism in SGA/Giraud; this specific application unpublished

ideas.what: Description of M_0 = _2E as V_J(F_2) = F_2^J/diag for the degree-3 cover J, and the exact functor V_J(A) = Ker(A^J -> A)
ideas.modern_name: GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 dictionary; Weil restriction/norm-kernel torus construction

ideas.what: Decomposition End(M_0) ≅ M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω as Galois modules, with ω the orientation (discriminant) double cover
ideas.modern_name: Projective indecomposable decomposition V⊗V ≅ V ⊕ P(1) for F_2[S_3]; Shapiro-lemma splitting of H^1

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, intrinsic, scheme-theoretic set-up of level-4 structures as level-2 data plus a torsor under End(_2E). The splitting End(M_0) = M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω is neat and correct, and gives a canonical decomposition of the lifting data. But all of it is routine for a specialist, and the level-4 Legendre-type moduli are classical. Nothing here seems absent from the literature in substance.
transcription_corrections: 'Une épi-glage [?] de M' should read 'Un épinglage de M' (a pinning/trivialization).
In the text before (40): 'd'un J [-rev.-] étale de degré 3 de S' — likely 'd'un J rev. étale de degré 3 de S', with a struck-out fragment after.
Marginal note: 'ω = rev. étale de degré 2 "des orientations" associé au rev. J de degré 3 de S' — consistent with the image; it attaches to (41).
(39) diagram: M_0 ↪ M (inclusion, labelled 'can'/'inj') and the arrow M -> M labelled 2 id_M; 'M ↪ [?]' is the vertical inclusion M_0 ↪ M.
(41) is written with opening quotation marks: '"V_J(M_0) ≃ End_{F_2,S}(M_0) ≃ M_0 ⊕ F_2^ω'.
The last line likely reads 'équivaut à : celle d'une trivialisation de J, plus d'une section (définie ...) de ce torseur', continuing on the next page.
